teaser: He reached Madinah two months ahead of the Prophet ﷺ. He died of a wound everyone thought had healed.
quran_mention: «إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ» — 'we belong to Allah and to Him we return' (al-Baqarah 2:156). Umm Salamah reported that the Prophet ﷺ taught her to say this at the death of Abu Salamah, and to ask Allah for a reward and for something better in its place.

layers.title: Who He Was
layers.subtitle: Cousin, foster brother, and son of Makhzum
layers.content:
His name was Abdullah, but he is known by his kunya: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad ibn Hilal, of Banu Makhzum — the clan of Abu Jahl and Khalid ibn al-Walid, one of the strongest houses in Makkah.

He was also close family to the Prophet ﷺ, twice over. His mother was Barra bint Abd al-Muttalib, which made him the Prophet's ﷺ cousin. And al-Mubarakpuri records that Thuwaibah, the freed slave of Abu Lahab, nursed the infant Muhammad ﷺ and later nursed Abu Salamah too, so that they were foster brothers as well.

He married Umm Salamah, Hind bint Abi Umayya ibn al-Mughira, of his own clan. Their children were Salama, Umar, Zaynab and Durra. Zaynab was born in Abyssinia, in the middle of the migration — a daughter with no memory of the city her parents came from.

Of the four names in that list, one would grow up in the household of the Prophet ﷺ himself. Umar ibn Abi Salamah is one of the reporters Ibn Sa'd relies on for his father's story.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: Two crossings of the sea with his wife
layers.content:
Yazid ibn Ruman puts him among the very earliest: Muslim before the Prophet ﷺ had begun using the house of al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam, before there was any organised call at all. A man of Makhzum, in the years when Makhzum was the sharpest edge of the opposition.

What it cost is measurable in journeys. Ibn Sa'd says that on this point all the sources agree: Abu Salamah went to Abyssinia twice, and both times he took Umm Salamah with him. Two crossings out of Arabia and two returns, a marriage carried across the sea and back, a child born in the second country.

They did not come home to safety. Makhzum was his own clan, and the persecution he was escaping was in part his own family's work. When the way opened to Madinah, he did not wait for a group to form, or for the Prophet ﷺ to move first. He went out on his own, ahead of everyone.
layers.source: Reported from Yazid ibn Ruman — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: First man of the hijrah to arrive
layers.content:
Muhammad ibn Umara ibn Khuzayma ibn Thabit reported what the people of Banu Amr ibn Awf remembered: the first man to reach us in the emigration from Makkah was Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad. He came on the tenth of Muharram. The Prophet ﷺ reached Madinah on the twelfth of Rabi' al-Awwal — two months later. And two months passed between Abu Salamah's arrival and the next Muhajir's.

So for eight weeks the entire emigration to Madinah consisted of one man. Amir ibn Rabi'a, who came next, put it in one line: nobody made hijrah to Madinah before me except Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad.

He stayed at Quba' with Mubashshir ibn Abd al-Mundhir. The Prophet ﷺ later joined him in brotherhood with Sa'd ibn Khaythama, and allotted him a house. He fought at Badr and at Uhud, and in Muharram of the fourth year the Prophet ﷺ put him in command of an expedition to the Banu Asad at Qatan. He was away about ten days.
layers.source: Reported from Muhammad ibn Umara ibn Khuzayma and Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabi'a — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: A wound that closed over and did not heal
layers.content:
At Uhud a man of the Jusham named Abu Usama put a spear into his upper arm. He was treated for a month. Ibn Sa'd's phrasing is careful: he was cured along with those who were cured. He went back into ordinary life as a healed man.

The wound had gone bad inside without his knowing it.

Some months later he took command of the expedition to Qatan and was on campaign for around ten days. He came back to Madinah and the arm began to trouble him again, and this time it did not stop. He fell ill and died on the twenty-seventh of Jumada al-Akhira.

There is nothing dramatic in it. He was not killed in the line at Uhud, which is the death the sources usually pause over. He was wounded there, told he was better, sent on duty, and then quietly killed by the same wound almost two years after he took it. The man who had been first out of Makkah and first into Madinah went out on a sickbed with an infected arm.
layers.source: Reported from Umar ibn Abi Salamah — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ himself closed his eyes
layers.content:
Qabisa ibn Dhu'ayb reported that the Prophet ﷺ came to him as he was dying, that a curtain was let down between them, and that they wept. When his breath stopped, the Prophet ﷺ put his hands over his eyes and closed them.

The women in the room began to speak, and he checked them: the angels are present at a death, and they say amin to what you ask, so ask only for good. Then he made the du'a himself — make his grave wide for him and light it for him, make his light immense, forgive him, raise his rank among those who guide, and appoint someone to take his place for what he has left behind. Then he said: when the spirit goes out, the eye follows it.

Umm Salamah kept her four months and ten days. That last request in the du'a was answered in the most direct way available: al-Mubarakpuri records that the Prophet ﷺ married her in Shawwal of the same year, 4 AH. She narrated afterwards that he had taught her to ask Allah for something better than what she had lost, and that she had wondered who could possibly be better than Abu Salamah.
layers.hadith_ref: The death of Abu Salamah and the du'a — reported from Qabisa ibn Dhu'ayb and Abu Qilaba, Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III. The du'a taught to Umm Salamah on affliction — Sahih Muslim, Book of Funerals, narrated by Umm Salamah
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

quiz.prompt: In what two ways was Abu Salamah related to the Prophet ﷺ?

options.text: Brother-in-law and neighbour
Cousin through his mother, and foster brother through the same wet nurse
Uncle and business partner
Son-in-law and cousin

quiz.citation: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III, on Barra bint Abd al-Muttalib; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar, on Thuwaibah
quiz.scholar_reflection: Thuwaibah was the freed slave of Abu Lahab. She nursed the Prophet ﷺ as an infant, and Hamzah, and later Abu Salamah.

quiz.prompt: What does Ibn Sa'd say all the sources agree on regarding Abu Salamah and Abyssinia?

options.text: That he never went
That he went once, alone
That he emigrated there twice, with Umm Salamah
That he settled there permanently

quiz.scholar_reflection: Their daughter Zaynab was born there during the migration. On several other Companions the reports disagree about the second crossing; on Abu Salamah they do not.

quiz.prompt: What was Abu Salamah the first to do?

options.text: To reach Madinah in the hijrah from Makkah
To recite the Qur'an publicly
To be wounded at Badr
To build a house at Quba'

quiz.citation: Reported from Muhammad ibn Umara ibn Khuzayma ibn Thabit — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He arrived on 10 Muharram. The Prophet ﷺ arrived on 12 Rabi' al-Awwal, and the next Muhajir came two months after Abu Salamah did.

options.text: A sword blow at the expedition to Qatan
The plague
His spear wound from Uhud, which had turned septic after appearing to heal
An arrow at Badr

quiz.citation: Reported from Umar ibn Abi Salamah — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Abu Usama al-Jushami had speared him in the upper arm at Uhud. He was treated for a month and cured along with the others, then led an expedition, then died of it.

quiz.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ say to the women speaking at Abu Salamah's deathbed?

options.text: That they should leave the room
That the angels are present and say amin, so they should ask only for good
That weeping was forbidden
That they should recite Surah Yasin

quiz.citation: Reported from Abu Qilaba — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He then prayed for a wide, lit grave, forgiveness, a raised rank among those who guide, and a successor for what Abu Salamah was leaving behind.

quiz.prompt: He left for Madinah alone, two months before anyone followed. What would it take for you to go first?

options.text: Certainty that it is right
Knowing others will follow
Having nothing left to lose where I am
I would rather be second

quiz.citation: Reflection on the arrival of Abu Salamah at Quba', 10 Muharram — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: For eight weeks the emigration to Madinah was one household. He had no way of knowing at the time whether anyone else would come.

quiz.prompt: He crossed to Abyssinia twice and came back twice, and never got to settle anywhere for long. What has moving cost you?

options.text: Friendships and community
Work, money or standing
A sense of where home is
I have never had to move

quiz.citation: Reflection on the two migrations to Abyssinia — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Their daughter Zaynab was born in Abyssinia. Some children of that generation had a birthplace their family could not return to and did not come from.

quiz.prompt: He was declared healed, went back to work, and the wound was quietly still there. What in you got called fixed too early?

options.text: Something physical I keep working through
A grief I said I was over
A relationship I patched instead of repairing
Nothing I am aware of

quiz.citation: Reflection on the account of Umar ibn Abi Salamah — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn Sa'd notes that the wound became septic while he was not aware of it. He did not ignore a warning; he was not given one.

quiz.prompt: The du'a at his deathbed asked Allah to appoint someone to take his place for those he left behind. Who would step into your place?

options.text: Family who would manage
Nobody, honestly, and that worries me
I have started making arrangements
I try not to think about it

quiz.citation: Reported from Abu Qilaba — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: It is worth noticing what the Prophet ﷺ prayed for at a deathbed. Not only forgiveness and light, but practical cover for the people the dying man was responsible for.

quiz.prompt: Umm Salamah was taught to ask for something better, and could not imagine anything better. When have you had to ask for a good you could not picture?

options.text: After a loss, without believing it
I ask for what I can picture and no more
I have asked and am still waiting
I find that kind of du'a difficult

quiz.citation: Sahih Muslim, Book of Funerals, narrated by Umm Salamah
quiz.scholar_reflection: She said the words while thinking that no one could be better than Abu Salamah. She was not required to believe the answer in advance in order to say the du'a.
